JAX.summary:
- **Travis Hunter (WR/CB)** — Jacksonville expects his defensive role to grow into something much closer to full-time cornerback duty, and the report says his offense won’t disappear, but his snap split should change materially from last year’s heavier wideout usage. That makes him a volatile fantasy piece: the ceiling is still there if the Jaguars keep him on the field at receiver, but the weekly volume path looks less stable [8].

- **Parker Washington (WR)** — The report frames Washington as an emerging three-level receiver who can handle multiple offensive roles, not just a special-teams job. For fantasy, that matters because it keeps him in the conversation for sub-package and complementary WR snaps if Jacksonville leans into his versatility [6].

- **Wyatt Milum (G) / Patrick Mekari (G)** — The left guard spot is one of Jacksonville’s few truly open starting jobs, with Milum viewed as the main challenger to Mekari. Mekari was described as the clear weak link a year ago, so this battle is worth watching because a Milum win would be the clearest OL upgrade path for a run game that “was nowhere near good enough” last season [2, 7].

GB.summary:
- **Chris Brooks (RB)** — Brooks has a real chance to win the No. 2 back job once he’s healthy; the report calls this the biggest opportunity of his career after three seasons mostly spent in pass protection and on special teams. MarShawn Lloyd is the main competition, so this is the Packers backfield battle that could matter most for early-down and handcuff value. [1]

- **Matthew Golden (WR)** — Golden is projected to open camp in the starting WR trio with Christian Watson and Jayden Reed, with the rest of the room bunched behind them. That gives the rookie a clear first-team role right out of the gate and puts him on the fantasy radar if he holds it. [1]

- **Luke Whyle (TE)** — With Tucker Kraft and Luke Musgrave unavailable at the start of camp, Whyle has a clear path to stake a claim as the No. 2 tight end. That matters because the rest of the depth chart is largely unproven, so any separation here could translate to meaningful snap and target opportunity. [1]
